concepts.title: Location and Physical Geography of the Amazon Basin

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Location and Physical Geography of the Amazon Basin' refers to.
questions.a: The equatorial geographic region in South America situated between 10 degrees North and 10 degrees South latitudes surrounding the Amazon river system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Location and Physical Geography of the Amazon Basin'.
questions.a: The Amazon drainage network forms the globe's largest river basin directly straddling the equator.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Location and Physical Geography of the Amazon Basin' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Life in the Amazon Basin (source: gess206.txt lines 20-50)

concepts.title: Climate and Biodiversity of the Amazon Rainforest

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Climate and Biodiversity of the Amazon Rainforest' refers to.
questions.a: A hot and wet tropical forest biome near the equator characterized by constant heavy rain, a thick foliage roof, epiphytic plants, and diverse fauna.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Climate and Biodiversity of the Amazon Rainforest'.
questions.a: Constant warmth and heavy precipitation nurture dense evergreen canopy layers and exotic species.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Climate and Biodiversity of the Amazon Rainforest' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Climate and Rainforests (source: gess206.txt lines 51-110)

concepts.title: Human Adaptation and Farming Practices in the Amazon Rainforest

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Human Adaptation and Farming Practices in the Amazon Rainforest' refers to.
questions.a: Forest settlement practices centered on slash-and-burn farming, root crops like manioc, communal Maloca housing, and modern highway impacts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Human Adaptation and Farming Practices in the Amazon Rainforest'.
questions.a: Shifting cultivation and traditional architecture adapt to rainforest conditions, though modern access leads to habitat depletion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Human Adaptation and Farming Practices in the Amazon Rainforest' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: People of the Rainforests (source: gess206.txt lines 111-160)

concepts.title: Geography and Climate of the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Geography and Climate of the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin' refers to.
questions.a: A subtropical Asian river basin located between 10 degrees North and 30 degrees North latitudes, characterized by vast alluvial plains, Himalayan mountain slopes, and monsoon seasons.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Geography and Climate of the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin'.
questions.a: Extensive lowlands fed by major Himalayan snowfed streams and seasonal monsoon currents support high settlement densities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Geography and Climate of the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Life in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin (source: gess206.txt lines 161-210)

concepts.title: Population Density Calculation in Regional Demography

questions.q: Find the population density when a total population of people lives in a square km area. Use the method 'Population Density Calculation in Regional Demography'. Work with: area = 250, population = 25000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of density.
questions.a: 100 persons per sq km

questions.q: Compute average human concentration per square kilometer for a given district. Use the method 'Population Density Calculation in Regional Demography'. Work with: area = 500, population = 60000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of density.
questions.a: 120 persons per sq km

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Population Density Calculation in Regional Demography' refers to.
questions.a: The mathematical measurement of human concentration calculated by dividing total headcount by the corresponding surface land area in square kilometers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Population Density Calculation in Regional Demography'.
questions.a: Dividing resident population count by territorial area yields average human spatial concentration.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Population Density Calculation in Regional Demography', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: density = population / area

concepts.title: Agricultural Systems and Terrace Farming in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Agricultural Systems and Terrace Farming in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin' refers to.
questions.a: Farming practices adapted to regional terrain, ranging from water-intensive paddy on plain alluvium to stepped terraces on mountain slopes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Agricultural Systems and Terrace Farming in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin'.
questions.a: Flat fertile plains enable high-yield paddy and cash crops while stepped hill terraces reduce soil water runoff.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Agricultural Systems and Terrace Farming in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Agriculture and Topography (source: gess206.txt lines 231-270)

concepts.title: Natural Vegetation, Wildlife and River Ecosystem Health

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Natural Vegetation, Wildlife and River Ecosystem Health' refers to.
questions.a: Diverse ecological zones containing deciduous forests, delta mangroves, mountain conifers, and bio-indicator fauna like the Susu dolphin.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Natural Vegetation, Wildlife and River Ecosystem Health'.
questions.a: Elevation variations govern natural flora while species like blind dolphins reveal river water purity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Natural Vegetation, Wildlife and River Ecosystem Health' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Vegetation and Wildlife (source: gess206.txt lines 271-330)

concepts.title: Urbanization, Transport Networks, Conservation and Tourism

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Urbanization, Transport Networks, Conservation and Tourism' refers to.
questions.a: Demographic centers along river corridors supported by multiple transit options, federal river restoration initiatives, and cultural heritage sites.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Urbanization, Transport Networks, Conservation and Tourism'.
questions.a: Dense riverfront cities stimulate trade and transport networks, necessitating conservation programs like Namami Gange.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Urbanization, Transport Networks, Conservation and Tourism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Cities, Transport and Tourism (source: gess206.txt lines 331-380)
